question.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1]\,,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

If $x(t)=k-2{t}^{3}$ and $y(t)=t$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product is equal to zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}t(k-2{t}^{3})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(kt-2{t}^{4})\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{k{t}^{2}}{2}-\frac{2{t}^{5}}{5}){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{2}-\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & =0 \\ \frac{k}{2}-\frac{2}{5} & =0 \\ \frac{k}{2} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ k & =\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
